writing.task: Task 1 · Museum Family Learning Day Table
writing.focus: Paraphrasing numbers and comparing activities with linked ideas
writing.prompt:
The table below shows information about four activities at a Museum Family Learning Day held at Riverside Museum on 16 March 2024. It shows the number of families, the total number of participants, and the average satisfaction rating (out of 5) for each activity.

Pottery Workshop: 42 families, 118 participants, rating 4.6
Storytelling Tour: 55 families, 142 participants, rating 4.8
Science Discovery Lab: 38 families, 105 participants, rating 4.3
Art Trail Challenge: 48 families, 130 participants, rating 4.5

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. You should write at least 150 words in about 20 minutes.

writing.task: Task 1 · Public Library Digital-Skills Sessions Bar Chart
writing.focus: Correcting details and making clear comparisons across age groups
writing.prompt:
The bar chart below shows the age-group distribution of attendees for three types of Public Library Digital-Skills Sessions at Greenfield Central Library in 2024. For each session type, it shows two figures, both expressed as a percentage of all attendees for that session type: (1) the share of attendees in each age group, and (2) the share of attendees in each age group who completed the follow-up practice task at home.

Basic Internet Safety – Share of all attendees: 16-25 years 35%, 26-50 years 45%, 51+ years 20%. Share of all attendees who completed task: 16-25 years 28%, 26-50 years 38%, 51+ years 12%.
Online Job Applications – Share of all attendees: 16-25 years 40%, 26-50 years 38%, 51+ years 22%. Share of all attendees who completed task: 16-25 years 32%, 26-50 years 30%, 51+ years 15%.
Video Calling Family and Friends – Share of all attendees: 16-25 years 15%, 26-50 years 30%, 51+ years 55%. Share of all attendees who completed task: 16-25 years 12%, 26-50 years 25%, 51+ years 40%.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. You should write at least 150 words in about 20 minutes.

writing.task: Task 2 · Museums and Family Learning Days
writing.focus: Paraphrasing views and linking ideas with reasons and examples
writing.prompt: Some people think museums should organise more interactive family learning days to attract visitors of all ages. Others think museums should mainly focus on protecting and displaying historical objects in a traditional way. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. You should write at least 250 words in about 40 minutes.

writing.focus: Presenting a clear position with corrected details and connected arguments
writing.prompt: Many universities hold a student volunteering fair where local charities offer projects such as tutoring, environmental clean-ups, and care for older people. Some people believe all students should be encouraged to do some volunteering, while others think students should focus only on their academic studies. Discuss both views and give your own opinion. Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. You should write at least 250 words in about 40 minutes.

writing.focus: Evaluating advantages and disadvantages with clear comparisons
writing.prompt: Public libraries in many towns now offer free digital-skills sessions, for example how to use email, online banking, and video calls. Do the advantages of this development outweigh the disadvantages? Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your own knowledge or experience. You should write at least 250 words in about 40 minutes.

speaking.focus: Paraphrasing familiar ideas and giving linked answers
speaking.prompt:
Let's talk about museums and learning with family.
Do you enjoy visiting museums? Why or why not?
Did you visit museums with your family when you were younger?
What kind of museum activities do you think children enjoy most?
Do you prefer learning by doing an activity or by reading information?

speaking.focus: Giving clear personal information with connected sentences
speaking.prompt:
Let's talk about helping and volunteering.
Have you ever done any volunteering? What did you do?
Do many young people in your area volunteer?
What kind of volunteering do you think is most useful for the community?
Would you like to take part in a volunteering fair at your school or university?

speaking.task: Part 2 · Cue card · A Family Learning Day
speaking.focus: Describing an experience with linked ideas and corrected details
speaking.prompt:
Describe a family learning day or educational visit you attended or would like to attend.
You should say:
• where and when it was or would be
• what activities were or would be available
• who you went with or would go with
• and explain why you found it enjoyable or why you would like to go.

You will have one minute to prepare and then speak for one to two minutes.

speaking.task: Part 2 · Cue card · A Digital Skill You Learned
speaking.focus: Explaining a learning process with clear comparisons and examples
speaking.prompt:
Describe a digital skill you learned in a library, community centre, or online session.
You should say:
• what the skill was
• where and how you learned it
• how difficult it was at first
• and explain how you have used this skill afterwards.

You will have one minute to prepare and then speak for one to two minutes.

speaking.focus: Giving reasons, evaluating ideas, and comparing views
speaking.prompt:
Let's discuss community learning more generally.
Why do some people prefer interactive learning days while others prefer learning alone?
What are the advantages for students of meeting charities at a volunteering fair compared to choosing a project online?
Do you think free digital-skills sessions in libraries can reduce differences between age groups? Why or why not?
How can museums, libraries, and volunteering projects work together to support local communities?
